title: Toolcall regression watchdog: per-config baselines and automated alerts for selection & arg fidelity
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: As we add model variants and new runtime/config knobs (quantization profiles, batching, kernel paths), we've seen subtle regressions in tool/function-calling behaviour: wrong tool selection when prompts are ambiguous, missing or malformed arguments, and inconsistent schema adherence. This ticket creates a regression-watchdog workflow that ties eval runs to every model/config change, produces per-config baselines for selection accuracy and argument validation, and triggers human/automation alerts when regressions cross defined thresholds. Goals: 1) Prevent rollouts that degrade tool-selection accuracy or argument correctness. 2) Provide per-config historical baselines and automated delta detection. 3) Integrate with Console dashboards and release gates.
acceptance_criteria: An automated nightly eval job runs the tool-calling harness across all model variants and quantization profiles listed in our model catalog.
Baseline metrics established per (model, quantization, runtime-config) including: tool selection accuracy, argument extraction F1, schema conformance rate, and calibration score.

A regression detector computes statistically-significant drops relative to baseline and generates an alert when: selection accuracy drops >= 5 percentage points AND p < 0.01 OR arg-validation F1 drops >= 7 percentage points.
Alerts create a Slack/Console incident, open a Linear ticket pre-populated with diagnostics, and attach the failing prompt subset and a link to replay logs.
Release gating: new model/config promotions to production are blocked if a canary run shows a regression above thresholds; documented override workflow exists.
Dashboard surfaces per-config time-series for the four core metrics and highlights anomalies with drilldowns into example prompts and model outputs.
E2E tests and unit tests cover the harness runner, delta computation, and alerting pipeline with deterministic seeds for reproducibility.
test_plan: Create a canonical eval dataset of 5k curated prompts with ground-truth tool labels and normalized argument schemas (includes edge cases and ambiguous prompts).
Build synthetic adversarial augmentation (+2k prompts) for argument fuzzing: missing fields, swapped types, nested arrays, unexpected enum values.
Nightly CI job runs full eval for accepted (model,config) matrix; compare to stored baselines and compute deltas with bootstrap confidence intervals.
Run targeted canary before release: 1% traffic mirror to candidate variant with live telemetry compared to baseline; fail-fast if detector trips.
Manual review workflow: PM/ML/Eng reviewers receive sample of failures and tag as false-positive/true regression to refine thresholds.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): implement harness runner and baseline store; run in readonly nightly mode to collect baselines.
Phase 2 (1 week): add statistical detector and basic Slack + Linear alert integration; run detector in dry-run mode with weekly review.
Phase 3 (1 week): enable automatic ticket creation and integrate with release gating for canary promotions.
Phase 4 (ongoing): refine thresholds, add more datasets, and instrument Console dashboard with drilldowns and replay links.
monitoring_queries: sql:SELECT model, config, date_trunc('day', ts) as day, avg(selection_accuracy) FROM eval_results GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY 3 DESC LIMIT 90
alert rule: WHEN delta_selection_accuracy <= -0.05 AND p_value < 0.01 FOR 1h THEN alert('toolcall-regression')
datasets: canonical_toolcall_set_v1 (5k curated prompts, ground-truth tool + args)
customer_sample_set_beta (anonymized customer prompts for high-impact surface area)

decision_notes: We prioritize low-latency nightly runs for breadth and a short canary for release-time safety. Statistical detector uses bootstrap CIs rather than simple % thresholds to reduce noise.
False positives will be suppressed via a reviewer-feedback loop that adjusts baselines when a failure is marked "non-regression" by two reviewers.
